# One CAD book over two years, holding every figure the two statements have to
# be able to print, and billing right through both so that any fiscal year cuts
# across the trading rather than lining up with it.
#
# Every top-level account is held in CAD, so the book is kept in CAD (Q-042).
# What happens:
#
# - 2025-04-01  20,000.00 CAD of opening capital.
# - 2025-05-05  10,000.00 USD bought for 13,000.00 CAD at 1.30, the cost basis
#               the later USD sale is measured against.
# - 2025-06-08  5,500.00 HKD bought for 1,000.00 CAD at 5.5 HKD per CAD.
# - 2025-07-12  4,000.00 USD borrowed, stated wholly in US dollars, so neither
#               the dollars nor the debt gets a cost.
# - 2025-08-15  20 NASDAQ:AMZN bought at 200.00 USD.
# - 2026-06-30  8 AMZN sold at 260.00 USD, taking 480.00 USD.
# - 2026-07-15  3,000.00 USD sold at 1.38 that cost 1.30, taking 240.00 CAD.
# - 2026-09-30  1,500.00 USD of the loan repaid with 100.00 USD of interest.
# - Fees: 50.00 CAD on 2025-12-20 and 150.00 CAD on 2026-12-20.
#
# Consulting is billed every quarter and collected a month later, except the
# last, which is still owed. Each quarter differs, so a fiscal year that ends
# anywhere picks up a different four:
#
#     2025-06-30  1,000.00      2026-03-31  1,600.00      2026-09-30  2,000.00
#     2025-09-30  1,200.00      2026-04-10    900.00      2026-12-31  2,200.00
#     2025-12-31  1,400.00      2026-06-30  1,800.00
#
# So the fiscal years a Canadian filer actually uses come out differently:
#
#     ending 2026-03-31   consulting 5,200.00, and no gain taken
#     ending 2026-04-25   consulting 6,100.00 — the 04-10 bill lands inside it
#     ending 2026-06-30   consulting 6,900.00, and the shares sold on the last day
#     ending 2026-12-31   consulting 8,500.00, both gains, and the interest
#
# What is still held at 2026-12-31: 19,840.00 CAD, 7,480.00 USD, 5,500.00 HKD,
# 12 AMZN and a 2,200.00 CAD receivable, against 2,500.00 USD still owed.
#
# Every transaction that spends US dollars the book keeps a cost basis for says
# which one they came out of, and that cost basis is a split the file assigned
# a guid of its own — the guid GnuCash would assign is not knowable while the
# file is being written, so a book that opens a cost basis and spends it in one
# file has no other way to point at it.
#
# The book is deliberately part-costed, which is what makes it worth keeping:
# only the 10,000.00 USD bought with Canadian dollars says what it cost, so the
# cost bases hold 3,480.00 USD against the 7,480.00 the bank holds, and the
# balance sheet leaves that currency to GnuCash's own revaluation and says so
# with `measured_from: gnucash_revaluation`. The borrowing, the share purchase
# and the share sale are all stated wholly in US dollars, with no Canadian
# figure in them to cost either side from. Nothing spends out of the owed side's
# cost bases either, because the loan was drawn the same way and has none.
#
# Prices, all at 12:00 UTC: USD in CAD 1.30 on 2025-05-05, 1.35 on 2026-03-31,
# 1.38 on 2026-07-15 and 1.42 on 2026-12-31; CAD in HKD 5.5 on 2025-06-08 and
# 5.0 on 2026-12-31; NASDAQ:AMZN in USD 200 on 2025-08-15, 260 on 2026-06-30
# and 280 on 2026-12-31.

	fraction: 10000

2025-04-01 * "Opening capital"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:CAD Bank 20000.00 CAD
	Equity:Opening CAD -20000.00 CAD

2025-05-05 * "Buy 10,000.00 USD at 1.30"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank 10000.00 USD
		guid: "dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0001"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "13000.00"
	Assets:CAD Bank -13000.00 CAD

2025-06-08 * "Buy 5,500.00 HKD at 5.5 per CAD"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:HKD Bank 5500.00 HKD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "HKD"
		share_price: "2/11"
		value: "1000.00"
	Assets:CAD Bank -1000.00 CAD

2025-06-30 * "Consulting billed, Q1"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Receivable 1000.00 CAD
	Income:Consulting -1000.00 CAD

# Stated wholly in US dollars, so there is no Canadian figure in it to say what
# either side cost, and neither side opens a cost basis. That is what the book
# is for: the dollars it holds are partly costed and partly not, which is the
# state `measured_from: gnucash_revaluation` describes on the balance sheet.
2025-07-12 * "Borrow 4,000.00 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:USD Bank 4000.00 USD
	Liabilities:USD Loan -4000.00 USD

2025-07-30 * "Consulting collected, Q1"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:CAD Bank 1000.00 CAD
	Assets:Receivable -1000.00 CAD

# Stated in Canadian dollars, so the dollars leave at what they cost and the
# shares arrive carrying it: 4,000.00 USD at 1.30 is 5,200.00 CAD, which is
# 260.00 a share. The entry balances by itself and realizes nothing, which is
# the truth of it — the dollars were exchanged for shares at their own cost.
2025-08-15 * "Buy 20 AMZN at 200.00 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:AMZN 20.0000 AMZN
		guid: "dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0004"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "AMZN"
		share_price: "260"
		value: "5200.00"
	Assets:USD Bank -4000.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-5200.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0001"

2026-06-30 * "Consulting billed, Q5"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Receivable 1800.00 CAD
	Income:Consulting -1800.00 CAD

# Stated in Canadian dollars, because a disposal that says nothing in the
# book's own currency cannot say what it realized. The shares leave at what
# they cost — 260.00 CAD each, being the 200.00 USD they were bought at carried
# through the 1.30 those dollars cost — the dollars they fetch arrive at the
# 1.35 of the day, and `$residual$` takes the 728.00 CAD between the two.
2026-06-30 * "Sell 8 AMZN at 260.00 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:AMZN -8.0000 AMZN
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "AMZN"
		share_price: "260"
		value: "-2080.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0004"
	Assets:USD Bank 2080.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "27/20"
		value: "2808.00"
	Income:Realized Gains $residual$ CAD

2026-07-15 * "Sell 3,000.00 USD at 1.38"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank -3000.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-3900.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0001"
	Assets:CAD Bank 4140.00 CAD
	Income:Realized FX Gains -240.00 CAD

2026-07-30 * "Consulting collected, Q5"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:CAD Bank 1800.00 CAD
	Assets:Receivable -1800.00 CAD

2026-09-30 * "Consulting billed, Q6"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Receivable 2000.00 CAD
	Income:Consulting -2000.00 CAD

# 1,600.00 US dollars leave the bank, so the bank split says which cost basis
# they came out of. The 1,500.00 of debt that goes with them is a disposal on
# the owed side and says nothing, because this book keeps no cost basis there:
# the loan was drawn in a transaction stated wholly in US dollars, which left
# the debt no Canadian cost to be measured against.
#
# `Expenses:Interest` is kept in US dollars, which gnucash-plaintext does not
# support: the 100.00 USD of interest was paid with dollars costing 1.30, so it
# cost 130.00 CAD, and both statements convert the account's balance at the
# sheet's own rate and state 142.00 instead. Both pages open with a warning
# saying so. This book keeps the account that way deliberately, being the book
# that shows what the warning is about. Its whole US dollar side falls back to
# GnuCash's revaluation, which prices that expense at the same 1.42, and the
# page balances. Kept in Canadian dollars at the 130.00 it cost, with this
# repayment written in them, it balances too, at the same total: 12.00 more of
# retained earnings and 12.00 less of unrealized gain.
2026-09-30 * "Repay 1,500.00 USD of the loan with interest"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Liabilities:USD Loan 1500.00 USD
	Expenses:Interest 100.00 USD
	Assets:USD Bank -1600.00 USD
		cost_basis_split_guid: "dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0001"

2026-10-30 * "Consulting collected, Q6"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:CAD Bank 2000.00 CAD
	Assets:Receivable -2000.00 CAD

2026-12-20 * "Bank fees"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Expenses:Fees 150.00 CAD
	Assets:CAD Bank -150.00 CAD

2026-12-31 * "Consulting billed, Q7, still owed at the year end"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Receivable 2200.00 CAD
	Income:Consulting -2200.00 CAD
